title: What narrative text adds to funding-speed forecasts
audience: Portfolio and industry readers, using a Kiva/partner decision case

slides.title:
What narrative text adds
to funding-speed forecasts
slides.subtitle: Post-competition research: matched full-data forecasts
slides.message: Measure what narratives add, then test whether a truthful change helps.
slides.evidence: 1,453,846 input records; 1,453,840 valid completed durations; 65 model/arm windows.
slides.visual: Minimal editorial cover, team names and recognition; no model-performance claim.
slides.action: Understand the project as a decision case with an explicit next test.
slides.notes: We are Mike Nguyen and Sophia Nguyen from Cultural Blend. This case began with a marketing question: which loan narratives are associated with faster funding? The maintained research now asks a more useful next question: what information does text add, and what evidence would justify changing how a loan is presented? We distinguish what the competition work established from later research. The new matched study is separate from the original competition results. The retrospective evaluation does not become an untouched test because we changed the protocol.

slides.title: Use the matched evidence to choose the next test
items: Training outcomes and completed-cohort membership precede each cutoff.
Structure and text use matching rows within each model family.
Check text meaning and intervention feasibility before a pilot.
slides.message: The next decision concerns measurement and intervention, informed by a completed comparison.
slides.evidence: Availability audit and fixed-config comparisons completed; no measured editing benefit.
slides.visual: Three large numbered statements on a flat canvas; no invented impact scores.
slides.action: Approve the research sequence before commissioning additional model complexity.
slides.notes: The first two research steps are now completed. This does not remove completed-record selection, snapshot-field uncertainty or construct validity questions. Decide what the remaining information gaps justify before choosing a writing or allocation policy.

slides.title: The outcome is completed funding on the platform
slides.message: The observed sample and timing determine what the project can claim.
slides.evidence: 1,453,846 input rows; six negative durations excluded; 1,453,840 eligible, including 1,637 refunded records. Dictionary reports 96.4% pre-disbursal.
slides.visual: Large eligible count at left, listing-to-completion timeline in text at right, precise population footnote.
slides.action: Interpret later results within completed records and distinguish borrower disbursal.
slides.notes: The full input contains 1,453,846 records from 2016 to 2025. Six negative durations are excluded. The analysis includes 1,637 refunded records with valid completed durations. The dictionary's full-data descriptive audit reports 96.4% pre-disbursal, so listing-to-completion time often begins after money has already been disbursed. It does not directly measure borrower waiting, partner liquidity or welfare. Unfunded and expired listings are needed to study all-listing success. The new as-of training audit removes pre-cutoff postings whose completed membership was not yet known; the primary August snapshot is preserved.

slides.title: Investigate four connected parts of the funding process
rows: Verified partner ID and process history
slides.message: Choose a mechanism to investigate before choosing a lever to change.
slides.evidence: Repository schema and Kiva process documentation; missing fields are data requests, not established causes.
slides.visual: Native editable issue-tree matrix with observed versus missing evidence.
slides.action: Prioritise the missing data required by the intended intervention.
slides.notes: This issue tree is a working decomposition. Its branches interact: a partner's process may affect both wording and exposure. Literature gives reasons to consider prosocial framing and lender preferences, while Kiva describes editing and translation in the posting process. None of these mechanisms is identified by a predictive importance chart. We should request data that can distinguish them.

slides.title: Text improves linear forecasts in all five years
slides.message: Matched gains quantify additional predictive information; they are not the effects of editing.
slides.evidence: Sparse Ridge/logistic family, fixed configurations, as-of training cohorts. Annual rows and exact metrics are in the reviewed bundle.
slides.visual: Native grouped MAE chart for all five years, with matched structure/text inputs.
slides.action: Assess the size and temporal stability of added predictive information.
slides.notes: Compare structure-only and structure-plus-text within the same sparse linear family, using the same rows, outcomes and cutoffs. TF-IDF is fitted on each training window only. The side callout is the median of annual MAE gains, not a loan-weighted pooled estimate. The AUC change is text-added minus structure-only in the latest observed year: a negative value means ranking declined even though duration MAE improved. These fixed models are not tuned winners. Description contents may encode context as well as framing.

slides.title: Read the added-text gain with its uncertainty
slides.message: Country-resampling intervals include zero in 4 of 5 linear comparisons; read both sensitivity checks.
slides.status: New matched comparisons; pointwise fixed-model sensitivity intervals
slides.evidence: Linear adds M+L+R; trees add M+L only. Positive gain means lower MAE in days. Month-cluster bootstrap uses 1,000 draws.
slides.visual: Native table of paired gains and month-block sensitivity intervals, with units.
slides.action: Choose a practical threshold with decision owners; do not infer an intervention return.
slides.notes: Each gain subtracts candidate absolute error from the structure-only error on the same records. Whole calendar-month blocks are resampled, preserving paired losses and weighting by record count. These are fixed-model sensitivity intervals, not causal intervals or retraining uncertainty. Annual windows have few independent month blocks. The notebook also shows country sensitivities, paired Brier gains and S+P versus S+P+text comparisons. P remains an unvalidated programme-text proxy.

slides.title: Large row counts do not remove contextual uncertainty
slides.message: Regional narrative patterns require careful treatment of the number of independent countries.
slides.evidence: Middle East slope −.0729, normal interval [−.1003,−.0456], heuristic [−.2502,.1043], 2 countries; Central America −.0742, normal [−.0879,−.0605], heuristic [−.1629,.0145], 2 countries. Slope units: change in log(1+days) per additional family mention per 100 words.
slides.visual: Two-region native table with point estimates, normal intervals and heuristic intervals. Clearly label the latter as uncalibrated sensitivity.
slides.action: Treat regional patterns as exploratory hypotheses, not country-specific writing advice.
slides.notes: The two regional point estimates suggest faster completed funding with more family mentions, conditional on the primary model. Each pooled region contains only two countries. The normal-reference country-clustered intervals and the much wider t(1) screen show why the uncertainty deserves attention. The screen is heuristic and is not a calibrated correction. In the same primary analysis, urgency has country-clustered p=.4943 for duration and .2233 for 24-hour completion. Failure to reject does not establish a negligible effect.

slides.title: Later checks retain some narrative associations
slides.after: Programme-adjusted business framing, 24-hour completion: −0.258 pp per additional mention / 100 words; 95% interval [−0.390, −0.126] pp; adjusted p = 0.00635.
slides.message: Statistical support changes with specification; a universal editing benefit remains unestablished.
slides.evidence: Same 1,453,840 eligible rows and 48 countries across four fits. Joint framing families remain associated. Primary predictive models were not rerun.
slides.visual: Compact specification comparison plus one clearly unit-labelled 24-hour result. Keep the two outcomes separate.
slides.action: Retire the blanket null story while retaining the intervention boundary.
slides.notes: The October extension is later research, separate from the competition submission. The third-person duration estimate changes modestly, while its adjusted p-value crosses .05. This is not proof that the association disappeared. Business framing is associated with a lower 24-hour completion probability under the programme specification. Several joint families remain associated. The programme variable is a text-derived proxy, not a verified partner ID. Coefficients are per extra mention per 100 words, and the duration outcome is log(1+days). Multiplicity is handled within each outcome/specification, not across the entire research history. Duration pointwise 95% intervals are [−0.013833, −0.004183] for expanded controls and [−0.013210, −0.002965] for programme adjustment. Business framing has a pointwise interval [−0.390, −0.126] percentage points. Intervals are pointwise; the displayed p-values are BH-adjusted within each outcome/specification.

slides.message: Prioritise learning value without inventing intervention returns.
slides.evidence: Synthesises current evidence boundaries. No cost or benefit estimates were collected.
slides.visual: Native options matrix using verbal judgments, no artificial impact scores.
slides.action: Prioritise construct validation and the feasibility of a defined pilot.
slides.notes: The audit and matched comparison are completed. They support a decision about further measurement and feasibility work, not a claim that changing text will improve funding. All-listing validation and an agreed operational purpose are still required for allocation tools. A model identifying slow loans does not identify who benefits from attention.

slides.title: Ranking and probability quality need separate checks
items: Population, as-of labels, feature blocks and validation contract.
Matched gains, calibration, error slices and text validity.
What is supported, what is uncertain and which test comes next.
slides.message: A ranking score cannot establish reliable probabilities for all new listings.
slides.status: 2025 observed completed records; sparse linear S+M+L+R
slides.evidence: Equal-width probability bins; empty bins omitted. Brier/log loss, counts, tail errors and group diagnostics are in the notebook.
slides.visual: Native line chart comparing predicted and observed probability within fixed bins.
slides.action: Inspect reliability, coverage and the population before considering an operational queue.
slides.notes: This diagnostic uses the latest observed year and the prespecified text-added sparse linear model. Predictions are compared with observed completion within 24 hours in the same probability bins, with counts shown below. Empty bins are omitted. The notebook compares both model families and shows duration-tail and novelty diagnostics. No calibration model has been fitted and no all-listing deployment evaluation has been performed.

slides.title: Test one truthful presentation change
slides.message: A prospective experiment should estimate a defined intervention on all eligible listings.
slides.evidence: Candidate factual clarity/specificity prompt, usual-content control. Assignment, horizon, practical threshold and power are not yet fixed.
slides.visual: Four numbered steps with endpoint and guardrails in a separate short statement.
slides.action: Agree the intervention and observation contract with participating partners.
slides.notes: One candidate is a prompt that makes the existing purpose and use of funds clearer while preserving facts. Compare the offer of that prompt with usual practice and include all eligible listings in analysis. Decide the assignment unit to limit staff/template contamination and marketplace spillovers. Choose one primary completion horizon, a practical effect threshold and sufficient independent units before launch. Do not compare duration only among loans that fund after treatment. Measure accuracy, editing burden, representation and displacement as guardrails. No sample size or duration is justified yet.

slides.title: Validate the proposed lever before running a pilot
slides.message: The retrospective comparison is complete; intervention benefit remains the next evidence gap.
slides.evidence: Research plan with dependency-based gates; no committed delivery dates.
slides.visual: Four horizontal work stages, owners and concrete exit tests.
slides.action: Validate narrative constructs and agree a feasible intervention design.
slides.notes: The as-of audit and matched full-data comparison are completed. Next validate the constructs, request historical field/exposure information and assess whether a factual presentation pilot is feasible. Agree its endpoint, assignment, practical threshold and guardrails before launch. The existing observational results do not establish the outcome of that experiment.
stages: Review constructs and historical field availability.

slides.title: Appendix: primary predictive benchmark
rows: Inspect tail error and loss alignment
Needs reliability analysis, not sufficient alone
slides.message: Keep metrics, target units and population together.
slides.evidence: Exact JSON report values; no rerun.
slides.visual: Native benchmark table with negative R² retained.
slides.action: Read complementary metrics and audit the prediction task before deployment.
slides.notes: Primary numeric values are read from the saved report. Ridge trains on log duration and is scored in days after exponentiation. This target/loss choice warrants inspection of tail predictions; a negative R² can coexist with a lower MAE than the baseline. The classifier's negative class is completed funding after 24 hours, not expired or never-funded listings. The historical holdout has already been examined and informed later research, so it is not a fresh untouched evaluation.

slides.message: Accurate language is part of analytical quality.
slides.evidence: Notebook/deck audit and current evidence map.
slides.visual: Two-column replacement table; historical materials remain preserved.
slides.action: Apply these replacements consistently in notebook prose and future slides.
slides.notes: Several old sentences are stronger than the data allow. The correction should be systematic rather than leaving a careful caveat at the end while overclaiming earlier. Also retire cross-unit coefficient rankings, the unsupported selectivity explanation for period trends, the 20,000-loan topic sample presented as full-data evidence, and claims that a heuristic few-cluster screen is calibrated inference. The missing comparison has now been run; its estimates remain predictive information gains.
